segments: 128 and eight months.
When he had killed Marwan,
he reigned alone over all the dominion of the Arabs.
And he abolished the kingdom from Damascus,
and transferred it to Babylon (Baghdad).
And from him was carried on the succession {OCR?} of Baghdad, whose kingdom in our days was brought to an end by the hand of the Huns, the Mongols.
It is related
that on a certain day, while this Abu'l-Abbas was encamped in one of the villages in the western region,
suddenly a great commotion fell upon his camp.
And all the people, and also the king himself, ran to see the marvel.
And when they went,
they saw eight men who had risen from the graves:
some of them up to their breasts,
some of them up to their loins,
and some of them up to their knees.
And among them were those whose beards were dyed, according to the custom of the Arabs;
and many people even recognized them.
And when they approached to speak with them,
they gave no answer at all.
And while they were amazed,
the king ordered that they should leave them for that day,
and that no one should approach them,
hoping that perhaps speech would be given to them.
And on the following day, when they went,
in the same manner they found {OCR?} them, alive and without speech.
Then he ordered, (and they died) and were buried a second time.
And in the year 1063
(1063 of the Greeks,
752 of our Lord?), the wife of King Constantine died, she who was the daughter of the Khagan.
And he remained three years without a wife,
according to the law of Christian kings.
Then certain deceitful men, under the guise of love, wished to cast him out from the kingdom,
and advised him to take a wife.
He, however, knowing their plot, said:
"I agree to your counsel.
Yet the law of the Romans has not slipped my mind,
and I also consider that it is not fitting for a king to become a slave to lust.
However, if you know that it is right,
make my son king in my place,
and I will yield to your wish."
And when he had placed the crown upon him,
he himself continued to direct the affairs of the kingdom,
because he was wise and feared by enemies.
And in that same year he went forth and attacked Melitene,
and set up catapults against it,
and breached a portion of its wall.
And at last he gave quarter to the Arabs who were in it,
and dismissed them.
And he deported the people of Claudias and of all the villages of Fourth Armenia.
